e.value:
- The insurer's sole stated basis is its internal policy MP-DME-031, which limits CGM coverage to Type 1 diabetes or Type 2 diabetes with ≥3 daily insulin injections or pump use. This policy directly conflicts with the 2024 ADA Standards of Care that recommend CGM for adults with Type 2 diabetes on any insulin therapy, including basal insulin alone [S7][S8].
- The denial claims fingerstick testing is an "adequate alternative," but multiple RCTs and systematic reviews demonstrate that real-time CGM significantly improves time-in-range and reduces HbA1c (by 0.4–0.5%) compared with self-monitoring of blood glucose in basal-insulin-treated patients [S1][S2][S4].
- The insurer's own referenced document (S5) sets a rigid injection-frequency threshold, yet the cited evidence (MOBILE trial, Martens et al.) specifically studied patients on once- or twice-daily basal insulin and found clinically meaningful HbA1c reductions with CGM [S2][S4].
- The denial labels CGM a "convenience item" despite ADA classifying it as a medical necessity for this population [S7] and evidence showing CGM reduces hypoglycemia risk without requiring bolus insulin initiation [S4][S6].
- No clinical rationale is provided for why the member's documented hypoglycemia unawareness (Z79.4) would not warrant CGM; the policy ignores this comorbidity entirely.

October 29, 2026

PACIFIC CREST HEALTH (Covered California Silver 87 HMO)
Member Services
2200 Harbor Blvd
Sacramento, CA 95814

Re: First-Level Internal Appeal – Claim PA-0930-77812
Member: Marcus Oyelaran
Denial Date: September 30, 2026
Service Denied: Continuous glucose monitor system and sensors (E2103, A4239)
Diagnoses: E11.65 (Type 2 diabetes with hyperglycemia), Z79.4 (Hypoglycemia unawareness)

I request that you reverse the medical-necessity denial and authorize coverage for a continuous glucose monitor (CGM) system and sensors for the above member.

The denial rests on three assertions, each contradicted by current clinical evidence and guidelines:

1. **Policy MP-DME-031 limits CGM to Type 1 diabetes or Type 2 diabetes with ≥3 daily injections or pump use.**  
   The 2024 ADA Standards of Care explicitly recommend CGM for adults with Type 2 diabetes on any insulin therapy, including basal insulin alone [S7][S8]. The ADA states CGM "should be offered for diabetes management in adults with diabetes on basal insulin who are capable of using the devices safely" [S8]. Your policy therefore conflicts with the nationally recognized standard of care.

2. **Fingerstick glucose testing is deemed an "adequate alternative."**  
   A systematic review of RCTs found real-time CGM significantly improves time-in-range and reduces HbA1c in insulin-treated Type 2 diabetes patients, including those on basal insulin [S1]. The MOBILE trial (N=175) demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically meaningful HbA1c reduction of −0.50% (95% CI −0.94 to −0.06; P=.02) with CGM versus self-monitoring in patients on once- or twice-daily basal insulin [S2]. Martens et al. reported a −0.4% HbA1c difference favoring CGM in basal-insulin-treated patients (P=0.02) [S1][S4]. These outcomes cannot be achieved with fingerstick testing alone.

3. **CGM is characterized as a "convenience item."**  
   The ADA classifies CGM as a medical necessity for this population [S7]. Evidence further shows CGM reduces hypoglycemia risk without requiring intensification to bolus insulin [S4][S6]. The member’s diagnosis of hypoglycemia unawareness (Z79.4) heightens the safety imperative for real-time glucose alerts, which fingerstick testing cannot provide.

Additionally, the injection-frequency threshold in your referenced document (S5) is not supported by the cited trials, which specifically enrolled basal-insulin-only patients and demonstrated benefit [S2][S4].

**Requests:**
- Provide the complete claim file, including the medical policy MP-DME-031 in effect on the denial date and the credentials of the reviewer who made this determination.
- Arrange a peer-to-peer review between the medical director and the member’s treating endocrinologist, Dr. [ATTACH: physician name and contact], to discuss the clinical necessity of CGM for this patient.
- If this appeal is denied, I will pursue an independent external review through the California Department of Managed Health Care as permitted by law.

I expect a written response within the plan’s standard timeframe. Please direct all correspondence to me at the address on file.

Sincerely,

Marcus Oyelaran

value.title: Send the appeal + request your claim file
value.detail: Mail or fax the letter with medical records attached. Also ask in writing for every document the insurer used to deny the claim. They must provide it free of charge.

value.title: Expedited decision due (72 hours)
value.detail: If you hear nothing by this date, call and ask for the decision in writing. Silence past the deadline can count as a denial you can escalate.

value.title: Ask your doctor for a letter of medical necessity
value.detail: A one-page letter from the treating clinician that addresses the specific criteria is the strongest attachment you can add.

value.title: External review deadline (if the appeal is denied)
value.detail: You have 4 months after a final internal denial to ask for an independent external review. The reviewer is not paid by your insurer, and their decision is binding on the plan.

value.title: Last day to file the internal appeal
value.detail: Your letter gives 180 days from the denial date.
